content_voiceover: This page covers ELN 2022 updates and targeted therapy pharmacology, both recurring exam favorites. Question six asks which changes from ELN 2017 to ELN 2022 are correct, and it's the first two. The FLT3 ITD allelic ratio was dropped from the risk model entirely, so a patient's risk category no longer depends on whether the ratio is high or low. And CEBPA mutant AML now qualifies as favorable based on having an in-frame mutation affecting the bZIP region, regardless of whether it's mono-allelic or bi-allelic, a shift from the old requirement of biallelic mutation. The other two statements are false, hyperdiploid karyotypes with multiple trisomies are actually excluded from the complex karyotype adverse category, not included, and AML with myelodysplasia related gene mutations, things like ASXL1, RUNX1, or SRSF2, is explicitly classified as adverse risk under ELN 2022, contrary to what the statement claims. Question nineteen repeats the FLT3 inhibitor pharmacology question, and the wrong statement is again the one that swaps type one and type two inhibitor mechanisms, type one inhibitors block both ITD and TKD mutations, type two inhibitors block ITD only.
keypoints: ELN2022 removed FLT3-ITD allelic ratio from risk stratification
CEBPA favorable prognosis now depends on bZIP in-frame mutation, mono or bi-allelic
Multiple trisomies or hyperdiploidy are excluded from the complex karyotype adverse group
Myelodysplasia-related gene mutations are classified as adverse risk in ELN2022
Type one FLT3 inhibitors block ITD and TKD; type two block ITD only
keypoint_voiceover: Two ELN2022 changes to nail down. The FLT3 ITD allelic ratio is gone from risk stratification, and CEBPA favorable status now just needs a bZIP in-frame mutation, mono or biallelic. On the flip side, multiple trisomies don't count as complex karyotype anymore, but myelodysplasia related gene mutations still land patients in the adverse risk group. And keep FLT3 inhibitor types straight, type one blocks both ITD and TKD, type two blocks ITD only.
